rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن is a biconsonantal conditional particle and also negates; grammarians dispute whether it governs like ما الحجازية. The author rejects equating it with إذا or weakened إن of إنّ.
rows.anchor: إن: حرف ثنائي الوضع يكون شرطا، وهو أصل أدواته، وحرف نفي، وفي إعماله إعمال ما الحجازية خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبد literally means a male human slave and derives in sense from worship, whose meaning was explained earlier.
rows.anchor: العبد: لغة المملوك الذكر من جنس الإنسان، وهو راجع لمعنى العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإتيان means coming; the command is ائت, whose form is unusual in both analogy and usage.
rows.anchor: الإتيان: المجيء، والأمر منه: ائت، كما جاء في لفظ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two unnamed poets' lines exemplify the anomalous deletion of the verb's initial radical in the imperative.
rows.anchor: وشذ حذف فائه في الأمر قياسا واستعمالا، قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سورة can mean a high rank: its reader is elevated above one who has not read it, as a wall rises above its surroundings.
rows.anchor: السورة: الدرجة الرفيعة. ألم تر أن الله أعطاك سورة؟ وسميت سورة القرآن بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed senses are completeness, like a fully formed she-camel, or a portion of Quran from أسأرت; Abu Ubayda says the original hamza was lightened, and hamza remains a dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لتمامها وكمالها، ومنه قيل للناقة التامة: سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likeness may consist in even the smallest degree of resemblance; Sibawayh says مررت برجل مثلك admits three interpretations.
rows.anchor: من مثله: المماثلة تقع بأدنى مشابهة، وقد ذكر سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثل must remain in a construct phrase; the author calls a poet's contrary usage a solecism and rejects the Kufan allowance that it can be غير مضاف.
rows.anchor: ولفظة مثل لازمة الإضافة لفظا، ولذلك لحن بعض المولدين في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الدعاء means calling out the name of the person invoked.
rows.anchor: الدعاء: الهتف باسم المدعو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شهداء is either an intensive plural of شهيد, like عليم/علماء, or a plural of شاهد, like شاعر/شعراء; the latter analysis is possible though less favored.
rows.anchor: الشهداء: جمع شهيد، للمبالغة، كعليم وعلماء، ولا يبعد أن يكون جمع شاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دون is an adverb of literal or figurative place and normally remains adverbial, used with the preposition من.
rows.anchor: دون: ظرف مكان ملازم للظرفية الحقيقية أو المجازية

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says the form دونك is never used as a nominative.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: وأما دونك فلا يرفع أبدا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says دونك and similar adverbs are not normally used as raised nouns, though they may sometimes be raised.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: وقد ذكر دونك وظروفا نحوها لا تستعمل أسماء مرفوعة على اختيار

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash allows inflection and treats ومنا دون ذلك as a subject that remains built because it is annexed to a built form.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قول الأخفش: جواز تصرفه، خرج قوله تعالى ومنا دون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poet attests to nominative poetic use of دون outside its usual adverbial construction.
rows.anchor: وباشرت حد الموت والموت دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When دون is an adjective meaning inferior, it can take varied inflections and is polysemous.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يعرب بوجوه الإعراب ويكون دون مشتركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh also records دون as an adjective meaning inferior or poor.
rows.anchor: وتجيء دون صفة بمعنى رديء، يقال: ثوب دون، أي رديء، حكاه سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is the opposite of lying and consists in a report matching what it reports about.
rows.anchor: الصدق: يقابله الكذب، وهو مطابقة الخبر للمخبر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن is a simple biconsonantal negator, not compounded from لا plus إن as al-Khalil reportedly held, nor does its ن replace an original alif as al-Farra held; it governs the subjunctive, though jussive use is reported.
rows.anchor: لن: حرف نفي ثنائي الوضع بسيط، لا مركب من لا إن خلافا للخليل في أحد قوليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن does not entail perpetual negation, contrary to one Zamakhshari view; it is not shorter-lived than لا, limited to the near future, extended like لا, or a supplication.
rows.anchor: ولا يقتضي النفي على التأبيد خلافا للزمخشري في أحد قوليه، ولا هي أقصر نفيا من لا

rows.speaker: ابن الطراوة
rows.claim: Some report jussive government by لن as a dialectal form; Ibn al-Tarawa cites a poem with يخب after لن.
rows.anchor: وذكروا أن الجزم بها لغة، وأنشد ابن الطراوة: لن يخب الآن من رجائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الوقود means fuel, what is used for kindling; it is also attested as a verbal noun, one of the rare nouns on the pattern فعول, alongside the forms listed by Ibn Asfur.
rows.anchor: الوقود: اسم لما يوقد به، وقد سمع مصدرا، وهو أحد المصادر التي جاءت على فعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحجارة is the plural of حجر, and its feminine ending emphasizes the feminine plural, as in الفحولة.
rows.anchor: الحجارة: جمع الحجر، والتاء فيها لتأكيد تأنيث الجمع كالفحولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعدت means prepared or made ready.
rows.anchor: أعدت: هيئت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the challenge was revealed about Jews who said Muhammad's message did not resemble revelation and that they doubted it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومقاتل: نزلت في اليهود، وسبب ذلك أنهم قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that the verse addresses all disbelievers rather than only Jews.
rows.anchor: وإن كنتم في ريب نزلت في جميع الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After arguing for God's oneness against shirk, the discourse addresses doubt about prophethood: the Quran is its proof as a miracle, tested by challenging eloquent Arabs and their allies to produce one surah.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها: أنه لما احتج تعالى عليهم بما يثبت الوحدانية ويبطل الإشراك

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Because the audience really was in doubt and إن conditions a possible or uncertain event, some exegetes say إن here means إذا; the author sides with the careful grammarians that إن never means إذا.
rows.anchor: ادعى بعض المفسرين أن إن هنا معناها: إذا، لأن إذا تفيد

rows.speaker: المبرد ومن وافقه
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and followers claim defective past كان retains special past force under إن, unlike other past verbs; the author sides with the majority that كان behaves like other past verbs.
rows.anchor: وزعم المبرد ومن وافقه أن لكان الماضية الناقصة معان حكما ليست لغيرها من الأفعال الماضية

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the conditional as an asserted fact, like a master telling a slave to obey if he is his slave, since God knows what hearts conceal; they connect it with the Jews' reported doubt.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين في قوله: وإن كنتم في ريب: جرى كلام الله فيه على التحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no need to make إن mean إذا: a past doubt can persist into the future, so the condition may mean if they continue in their prior state, like a parent warning a disobedient child.
rows.anchor: ولا تنافي بين إن كانوا في ريب فيما مضى وإن تعلق على كونهم في ريب في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author previously reconciled لا ريب فيه with وإن كنتم في ريب by treating the abstract meaning of doubt as if it were a concrete object.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم لنا أنه لا تنافي بين قوله تعالى: لا ريب فيه وبين قوله: وإن كنتم في ريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من can mark source or cause here, but not partitive; ما is relative, with a deleted object pronoun referring to what was sent down, though some take ما as an indefinite described noun.
rows.anchor: ومن تحتمل ابتداء الغاية والسببية، ولا يجوز أن تكون للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubling in نزلنا here is causative, equivalent to the transitive form أنزلنا, as supported by Yazid ibn Qutayb's reading مما أنزلنا.
rows.anchor: ونزلنا التضعيف فيه هنا للنقل، وهو المرادف لهمزة النقل

rows.speaker: يزيد بن قطيب
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Qutayb reads مما أنزلنا with form IV, which supports the author's view that the form II here marks causative transitivity rather than repeated or gradual descent.
rows.anchor: قراءة يزيد بن قطيب مما أنزلنا بالهمزة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says the form II signifies staged, successive revelation, a figurative sense prompted by the challenge; the author rejects that reading.
rows.anchor: خلافا للزمخشري، قال: فإن قلت لم قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intensive doubling usually affects already transitive verbs; since نزل was intransitive, its doubled form gains transitivity by causation, not repetition. Even rare intensive doubling of an intransitive remains intransitive, as مات المال/موت المال.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذهب إليه الزمخشري في تضعيف عين الكلمة هنا، هو الذي يعبر عنه بالتكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If نزلنا meant repeated gradual descent, لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة would require a strained interpretation; the cited requests for a sign and a messenger likewise mean sending down in general, not repetition.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فلو كان التضعيف في نزل مفيدا للتنجيم لاحتاج قوله تعالى: لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings with form II and form IV in many comparable passages, plus cases where repeated or gradual action is implausible, show that both forms can simply mean sending down.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فالقراءات بالوجهين في كثير مما جاء يدل على أنهما بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نزلنا shifts from the earlier address to plural first-person speech, magnifying the revelation and its recipient; the majestic نا intensifies this effect.
rows.anchor: وفي نزلنا التفات لأنه انتقال من ضمير الغائب إلى ضمير المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With revelation, على conveys that it is set over and firmly associated with its recipient, unlike إلى, which marks endpoint and arrival.
rows.anchor: وتعدي نزل بعلى إشارة إلى استعلاء المنزل على المنزل عليه وتمكنه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran repeatedly uses على for revelation, as in references to the Book sent down to the Prophet and the Quran sent down to bring no hardship.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى: نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Prophet God's servant honors him, marks exclusive devotion, and raises his rank; عبد may be generic or specific, and here is the specific, most honored sense.
rows.anchor: وفي إضافة العبد إليه تعالى تنبيه على عظيم قدره، واختصاصه بخالص العبودية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On the plural reading عبادنا, Zamakhshari says it may mean the Messenger and his community, since the guidance and promised benefit of revelation extend to followers as well as the Prophet; this is figurative inclusion of those charged with its commands as direct recipients.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ: على عبادنا بالجمع، فقيل: يريد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته، قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural could instead refer to the prophets who received revelation and scripture, with the Messenger foremost because his opponents challenge his book; the context addresses deniers of prophethood.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد به النبيين الذين أنزل عليهم الوحي، والكتب والرسول أول مقصود بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural may also use the singular generically, as in a singular reading of the plural expression about Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: وتبينه هذه القراءة كقوله تعالى: واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are asked for any surah, a Quranic unit of at least three verses, rather than a long one; this makes the challenge easy and maximally exposes and shames their inability.
rows.anchor: فأتوا بسورة: طلب منهم الإتيان بمطلق سورة، وهي القطعة من القرآن التي أقلها ثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they and their helpers cannot produce even one surah like it, they have no grounds to claim it belongs to their kind of speech or doubt its divine origin.
rows.anchor: فإذا كنتم لا تقدرون أنتم ولا معاضدوكم بالإتيان بسورة من مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem calls being addressed as the servant of the beloved the speaker's most honorable name.
rows.anchor: لا تدعني إلا بيا عبدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in مثله most likely refers to the revealed Quran, as most exegetes hold: the challenge concerns the revelation, parallels challenges to produce ten surahs like it and to produce its like, and tests all challengers together or individually, literate or not.
rows.anchor: من مثله: الهاء عائدة على ما، أو على عبدنا، والراجح الأول وهو قول أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls من مثله a modifier of سورة and glosses it as a surah belonging to the same kind; the author notes that syntactic attachment and adjectival relation are not the same analysis.
rows.anchor: من مثله متعلق بسورة صفة لها، أي بسورة كائنة من مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Zamakhshari's wording contradictory if متعلق means syntactic government but صفة means only relation to its noun; he salvages it as semantic attachment and distinguishes it from attaching من to فأتوا.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من كلام الزمخشري تناقض في من هذه قال: من مثله متعلق بسورة

rows.speaker: المهدوي وابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi and Ibn Atiyya allow من to be explanatory, if the pronoun refers to the revealed Quran; likeness then concerns its composition, eloquence, known meanings, or its unseen reports and truth, and they also allow an extra من.
rows.anchor: وأجاز المهدوي وأبو محمد بن عطية أن تكون لبيان الجنس على تقدير أن يكون الضمير عائدا على المنزل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari discusses the benefit of dividing the Quran into surahs; the author says that belongs to the benefits of division and is not tafsir.
rows.anchor: وقد تعرض الزمخشري هنا لذكر فائدة تفصيل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's grammatical school denies that من can mark explanation; من cannot be extra here according to the Kufans and most Basrans.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه أصحابنا أن من لا تكون لبيان الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account of likeness to the Quran is its excellent arrangement, striking composition, rare style, brevity, and perfected meanings.
rows.anchor: من مثله في حسن النظم، وبديع الرصف، وعجيب السرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account is likeness in its knowledge of unseen matters, reporting what happened and what will happen.
rows.anchor: من مثله في غيوبه من إخباره بما كان وبما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account is the Quran's range of commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, stories, judgments, exhortations, and parables.
rows.anchor: في احتوائه على الأمر، والنهي، والوعد، والوعيد، والقصص، والحكم، والمواعظ، والأمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth account is its truth and freedom from alteration or corruption.
rows.anchor: من مثله في صدقه وسلامته من التبديل والتحريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth account takes likeness to mean the speech of the Arabs, which is of the same linguistic kind.
rows.anchor: أي كلام العرب الذي هو من جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth account says repetition never makes it stale, tires its listeners, erases it, or exhausts its freshness, marvels, and sweetness.
rows.anchor: لا يخلق على كثرة الرد، ولا تمله الأسماع، ولا يمحوه الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh account is the lasting presence of its verses and the abundance of its miracles.
rows.anchor: من مثله في دوام آياته وكثرة معجزاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An eighth account compares it to prior revealed books, which could testify that this message is not from God; the passage invokes the demand for proof.
rows.anchor: الثامن: من مثله، أي مثله في كونه من كتب الله المنزلة على من قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun refers to the Messenger, من may attach to فأتوا and mark source, or modify an omitted noun to mean a surah originating from a man like him.
rows.anchor: وإن جعلنا الضمير عائدا على المنزل عليه، فمن متعلقة بقوله: فأتوا من مثل الرسول بسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view of likeness to the Messenger is to a naturally illiterate man unable to write.
rows.anchor: الأول: من مثله من أمي لا يحسن الكتابة على الفطرة الأصلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is a man like him who never studied with scholars, sat with sages, dealt in reports, or traveled beyond his town.
rows.anchor: الثاني: من مثله لم يدارس العلماء، ولم يجالس الحكماء، ولم يؤثر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is someone like what the opponents claimed he was: a sorcerer, poet, or madman.
rows.anchor: الثالث: من مثله على زعمكم أنه ساحر شاعر مجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view is a man from the Messenger's own kind and people.
rows.anchor: الرابع: من مثله من أبناء جنسه وأهل مدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likeness to the Quran is hypothetical under nearly all proposed senses, but not if it means Arab speech; likeness to the Messenger is actual because such people existed.
rows.anchor: وذكر المثل في قوله: من مثله هو على سبيل الفرض على أكثر الأقوال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says there is no actual peer: the Quran challenge asks for a surah with its rare eloquence, while a Prophet referent asks for someone with his Arab, human, or unlettered traits, without naming a counterpart.
rows.anchor: واختار الزمخشري أن لا مثل ولا نظير. قال بعد أن فسر المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Zamakhshari's no-peer claim: people sharing the cited traits of being human, Arab, or unlettered existed, and some Quranic likenesses are also possible.
rows.anchor: لأن المماثل في هذا الشيء الخاص موجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge requires them to summon witnesses or helpers so they can join efforts and support one another, rather than merely claim inability or ability alone.
rows.anchor: لم يكتف بقولهم ذلك بأنفسهم، حتى طلب منهم أن يدعوا شهداءهم على الاجتماع

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham explains دعاء here as seeking help or aid.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم: الدعاء طلب الغوث، دعا: استغاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دعاء can also mean summoning or presenting someone, as when a person is called before a judge.
rows.anchor: وباستحضروا دعا فلان فلانا إلى الحاكم، استحضره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل والفراء
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Muqatil, and al-Farra identify the witnesses as the idols, whom the opponents believed would testify for them before God.
rows.anchor: وشهداؤهم: آلهتهم، فإنهم كانوا يعتقدون أنهم يشهدون لهم عند الله، قاله ابن عباس، والسدي، ومقاتل، والفراء

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba takes the witnesses to be those they can summon and bring as helpers and supporters.
rows.anchor: أو من يشهدهم ويحضرهم من الأعوان والأنصار، قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Mujahid and Ibn Abbas identifies them as witnesses who could attest that the opponents' production matches the Quran.
rows.anchor: أو من يشهد لكم، أن ما تأتون به مثل القرآن، روي عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شهيد is the better plural source than شاهد because فعيل regularly forms فعيلاء and suggests emphatic, legally sufficient testimony.
rows.anchor: وكونه جمع شهيد أحسن من جمع شاهد لجريانه على قياس جمع فعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من دون الله may modify ادعوا, calling for witnesses apart from God rather than taking God as witness, or may attach to شهدائكم.
rows.anchor: من دون الله: تتعلق بادعوا، أي وادعوا من دون الله شهداءكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses may be the idols they took as gods apart from God, whom they claimed would testify that they were right on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: ادعوا من اتخذتموهم آلهة من دون الله وزعمتم أنهم يشهدون لكم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can mean their helpers apart from God, specifically apart from God's allies whom they rely on.
rows.anchor: أو أعوانكم من دون الله، أي من دون أولياء الله الذين يستعينون بهم دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من دون الله may mean before God; al-A'sha uses دون for in front of something, describing a mote visible through transparent material.
rows.anchor: أو يكون معنى من دون الله: بين يدي الله، كما قال الأعشى: تريك القذى من دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God knows they cannot meet the challenge, the order to produce a surah and summon allies is mockery and disabling; it is especially taunting if their witnesses are mute idols.
rows.anchor: وأمره تعالى إياهم بالمعارضة وبدعاء الأنصار والأعوان، مع علمه أنهم لا يقدرون على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صادقين may mean truthful in doubting the revelation's divine origin, or truthful in claiming they can rival it; the latter follows because they assume a nondivine text is challengeable.
rows.anchor: فظاهر قوله: إن كنتم صادقين معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they cannot meet the challenge, the discourse turns from mockery to guidance, ordering them to avoid the fire prepared for those who deny.
rows.anchor: انتقل إلى إرشادهم، إذ ليسوا بقادرين على المعارضة، وأمرهم باتقاء النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن rather than إذا continues the taunting challenge, like a speaker certain to win, or matches the opponents' own uncertainty before they reflect on the miracle and rely on eloquence.
rows.anchor: وأتى بإن، وإن كان من مواضع إذا تهكما بهم، كما يقول القائل: إن غلبتك لم أبق عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فإن لم تفعلوا means if you do not bring a surah; فعل is a general stand-in for any act and avoids spelling out the full phrase.
rows.anchor: ومعنى: فإن لم تفعلوا فإن لم تأتوا، وعبر عن الإتيان بالفعل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says فعل replaces الإتيان to avoid repeating the longer challenge wording; the author objects that إتيان could also be elided in both clauses, so the phrases are equivalent in ellipsis.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: لو لم يعدل عن لفظ الإتيان إلى لفظ الفعل لاستطيل أن يقال

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya oddly says لم is jussive because it resembles لا in negation: just as لا removes a noun's nunation, لم removes the verb's inflectional marker.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن عطية تعليل غريب لعمل لم الجزم، قال: وجزمت لم لأنها أشبهت لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future challenge stirs their determination so their ensuing inability will be more striking; it proves prophethood both through the Quran's inimitability and the prediction that they will never match it.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: ولن تفعلوا إثارة لهممهم ليكون عجزهم بعد ذلك أبلغ وأبدع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Foreknowledge that the opponents would never meet the challenge belongs only to God; their failure to produce or report an answer despite hostile motives confirms the prediction as a miracle.
rows.anchor: الإخبار بالغيب من أنهم لا لن يفعلوا، وهذا لا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musaylima and al-Mutanabbi did not attempt a literary counterchallenge; they claimed their crude, shallow, hybrid, badly composed texts were revelation, and God stripped them of eloquence for lying about Him.
rows.anchor: وأما ما أتى به مسيلمة الكذاب في هذره، وأبو الطيب المتنبي في عبره ونحوهما، فلم يقصدوا به المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولن تفعلوا is an inserted clause with no syntactic position; it strengthens the prediction that the conditional failure will certainly occur, and its particle لن distinguishes it from a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وقوله: ولن تفعلوا جملة اعتراض، فلا موضع لها من الإعراب، وفيها من تأكيد المعنى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says لن emphasizes future negation more strongly than لا, like a speaker's emphatic insistence; the author notes this conflicts with his other claim that لن negates forever.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره هنا مخالف لما حكي عنه أن لن تقتضي النفي على التأبيد

rows.speaker: ابن خطيب زملكاني
rows.claim: Ibn Khatib Zamalakani says لن negates something near and does not extend indefinitely, nearly reversing Zamakhshari's account.
rows.anchor: وأما ما ذهب إليه ابن خطيب زملكي من أن لن تنفي ما قرب وأن لا يمتد النفي فيها
